column1: # larger-BK + swizzled MMA shared (dot habu-mma-larger-bk, lib/ptx/cg-mma.f): padding As to a bank-conflict-free row stride unlocks the ldmatrix (fragment mode 2) load path, +54.8% over the BK=32 scalar baseline (398.5 -> 616.9 GFLOP/s at 2048^3), beating the FP32 MM kernel (441.8). All configs element-exact (tools/ptx/mma-gemm-check.f); measured by tools/ptx/gemm-bench.f GB-MMM-SWEEP. Re-measure at 918 MHz to refresh the shipped orin-nx-25w MMM / competitive golden (residual).

column1: # 918 MHz pinned re-measure of the MMA sweep (dot habu-re-measure-mma-9fe40cd1): the orin-nx-25w-408mhz rows above are same-session RELATIVE-correct but ~half absolute; these re-measure the identical configs with the GPU devfreq pinned min=max=918 MHz (25W mode-3 unchanged; restored to the as-found 408 MHz pin after), the historical measurement clock. Validation: the BK=32 baseline (885794) and FP32 MM (981225) reproduce the shipped 2026-07-14 orin-nx-25w MMM 884889 / MM 979866 within 0.15%, so the pin equals the shipped clock. The swizzle win is clock-independent and holds at 918 MHz: MMM-SWZ +53.4% and MMM-SWZ-BK64 +54.6% over the BK=32 baseline, both beating FP32 MM. Two runs, +/-0.1%; mma-gemm-check element-exact at the pin (4096+16384 cells, every config). Competitive note: the shipped HABU-MMM-TF32 row (tools/eval-triton.f) tracks the DEFAULT scalar+cvt kernel = 884889 (reconfirmed here), so it is left unchanged; the swizzled 1369587 is 72.4% of Triton 1890500 (vs the baseline 46.8%) but refreshes the competitive row only when the emitted default flips to pad=8 ldmatrix (separate default-flip dot).
